description: Lists every ticker we track, active or delisted, with its identity. For everything about one, use Get a ticker.

active.description: `true` for tickers that trade today, `false` for delisted ones. Omit it for both.

asset_class.description: Filter by asset class: `stocks`, `rates`, `crypto`, `fx` or a comma-separated list (the live classes today; validated for shape, not against a fixed list, so a well-formed class outside these matches nothing). Omit for every class. This is the class of instrument, distinct from `asset_type` below (the instrument type within equities). Every result carries its `asset_class`, so a non-equity result identifies itself.

asset_type.description: Filter by instrument type within equities (one or a comma list): the stored `asset_type` value (`CS`, `ETF`, `ADRC`, `PFD`, `FUND`, `UNIT`, `SP`, `ETS`, `WARRANT`, `RIGHT`, `ETN`, `ETV`), matched case-insensitively. `equity` is a convenience value expanding to the equity-like set. This is not an asset class: `asset_type=crypto` is a 400 (use `asset_class=crypto`). Values: CS, ETF, ADRC, PFD, FUND, UNIT, SP, ETS, WARRANT, RIGHT, ETN, ETV, equity.

cursor.description: The previous response's `next_cursor`. Send it with the same params as the first page (`limit` may change); a page whose params differ is a 400 naming the param.

exchange.description: Filter by exchange name (one or a comma list): the value results carry in their `exchange` field. MIC codes (`XNAS`, `XNYS`, `BATS`) are also accepted and match `exchange_mic`. A malformed value (non-letters, over 16 chars) is a 400.

limit.description: Page size. Max 1000 until 2027-01-12, then 100 (a larger value is clamped to the max, not an error; see Deprecations).

search.description: Case-insensitive match on `ticker` or `name`, max 64 characters (longer is a 400). Results are ranked: an exact ticker match first, then symbols that start with the term, then symbols that contain it, then names that have it as a whole word, then names that contain it; alphabetical within each rank. The cursor carries the rank, so paging a search never repeats or skips.

ticker.description: One symbol or a comma-separated list (up to 50; more is a 400): just those tickers' identity records, in the usual order. A symbol we don't track is absent from `results` and listed in `not_found`. For everything about each one, put the list in the path of Get a ticker.

name: tickerbot_list_tickers
